title: Glory in kindness (Jeremiah 9:22–23)
hookLine: let no one glory in wisdom, might or riches, but in knowing the God of kindness and justice
carry: here, in kitchens and courts and streets
last: HE STAYS, AND HE HURTS WITH THEM.

cards: Scroll any feed for a minute and the boasts sort themselves into three piles. Look how smart I am: the degree, the hot take, the clever reply. Look how strong I am: the workout, the win, the promotion.
Look how much I have: the car, the kitchen, the trip. The piles have changed their clothes over the centuries, but not their shape.
Jeremiah names all three in one breath, and then tells you the one thing worth boasting about. It isn't any of them.

teach.h: NOT WISDOM, NOT MIGHT, NOT RICHES.
teach.b: Here's the verse. "Thus saith the LORD, Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, neither let the mighty man glory in his might, let not the rich man glory in his riches." Wisdom, might, riches: the three piles.
The verse doesn't say they're bad. Being wise is good; strength is useful; money can do a lot. They're just not what to glory in.

"But let him that glorieth glory in this, that he understandeth and knoweth me, that I am the LORD which exercise lovingkindness, judgment, and righteousness, in the earth: for in these things I delight, saith the LORD."
Three Hebrew words: chesed, kindness; mishpat, justice; tzedakah, righteousness. Three boasts out; three of God's ways in. And look at the strange shape of the boast.
It isn't I am kind. It's I know a God who does kindness. To know God, in this verse, is to understand what God does and delights in.
In the earth: not only in heaven, but here, in kitchens and courts and streets.
In the last chapter of his Guide for the Perplexed, the philosopher Maimonides turns to this very verse.

His reading, in brief: knowing God leads somewhere practical, to acting with kindness, justice and righteousness yourself. So a ban on bragging becomes a job description, and that knowing is meant to show in the hands.

how: These verses close the haftarah read in synagogue on the morning of Tisha b'Av, so the day of mourning's reading from the Prophets ends on kindness, justice and righteousness.

o: wisdom, the first thing worth boasting of
kindness, one of the ways God delights in
strict justice, giving each what they earned

games.q: you're allowed one thing to boast about. which does Jeremiah's verse pick?
o: that you know the God of kindness and justice.
games.why: let him that glorieth glory in this, that he understandeth and knoweth me: kindness, justice and righteousness in the earth.

practice: Think back over the last few days and find one moment of kindness you saw, or were given, or managed to give: someone held a door, covered a shift, said the right word.
Hold it for a moment, and let it be the thing that matters about your week. If you pray, you can hold Jeremiah's words: for in these things I delight.
